name: landing-zone-core
description: Foundational resource-group scaffolding: hub VNet + NSG, Log Analytics, hardened Storage, and Key Vault. The shared base other workloads build on.
what: A minimal but production-shaped platform foundation: a hub virtual network with a default subnet and NSG, a Log Analytics workspace for centralized diagnostics, a hardened Storage account, and an RBAC-enabled Key Vault.
why: Every workload needs the same handful of shared services - somewhere to send logs, store state, and keep secrets, inside a governed network. Standing these up once, consistently and as code, prevents snowflake environments and gives every downstream use case a known-good base.
potentialUseCases: Bootstrapping a demo or MVP subscription before deploying workloads
A shared services resource group that multiple app teams build on
Teaching the landing-zone concept (logging, secrets, network segmentation) in a lab
A starting point you extend with private endpoints and policy for regulated workloads

reliability: Regional Log Analytics workspace for durable diagnostics
Storage account defaults are durable (LRS dev / ZRS or GRS prod)
Network segmentation via dedicated subnets and NSG
security: Key Vault with RBAC authorization and soft delete
Storage hardened: TLS 1.2, HTTPS-only, no public blob access
NSG governs subnet traffic; private workloads deploy into the hub VNet
costOptimization: Mostly consumption-based (logs, storage, secret ops) - pay for what you use
VNet and NSG incur no standing charge
Log Analytics retention tuned to 30 days by default
operationalExcellence: Single IaC entry point for the shared platform
Centralized logging endpoint for all workloads
performanceEfficiency: Workspace-based telemetry scales without capacity planning
Storage and Key Vault are fully managed PaaS
